## ⚠️ 25 March 1750/1 — Anomalous Double Date

The tool confirms this date is **outside the normal double-dating window** and flags it as anomalous. Here's why, and what to do.

---

### How double-dating normally works

In England before September 1752, the legal year began on **25 March** (Lady Day). That created a gap between the Old Style (OS) year and the modern New Style (NS) year for dates falling **1 January – 24 March**. Clerks resolved the ambiguity by writing *both* years, e.g.:

> **24 March 1749/50** → OS year 1749, but NS year 1750 → use **1750** in modern notes

---

### Why 25 March is different

**March 25 is the exact day the Old Style year turns over.** On that date, OS and NS *agree* — there is no ambiguity to resolve:

| Date | Old Style year | New Style year |
|---|---|---|
| 24 March | 1750 (last day of OS 1750) | 1751 |
| **25 March** | **1751** (first day of OS 1751) | **1751** |

A slash on 25 March is therefore anomalous — **both calendar systems say it's the same year**, so there is nothing to double-date.

---

### What the clerk probably meant

There are two plausible explanations:

1. **The entry is truly 25 March 1751 (NS = OS).** The clerk wrote the slash out of habit or caution at the year-turn boundary. → Use **1751**.
2. **The entry belongs to 24 March** (the last day of OS 1750), and the day was written one off. → Would be "24 March 1750/1" = **1751 NS**. Still use **1751**.

Either way, **1751** is the most defensible modern year for this marriage.

---

### What to do before deciding

> Check the **surrounding entries** in the register. Look at the entries just before and just after this one — does the clerk increment the year label on 25 March, or before it? That context will confirm whether this entry was treated as the last record of OS 1750 or the first of OS 1751.

---

### How to cite it in your research notes

Preserve the document exactly as written, then add your interpretation:

> Marriage of [names], **25 March 1750/1** (as recorded — anomalous double date at the OS year-turn; interpreted as **25 March 1751 NS**).

That way your notes are transparent about both what the record says and how you resolved it.
